items.title: Trump's Stablecoin Gains Merchant Acceptance
points: Trump's stablecoin (a cryptocurrency pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar) will soon be spendable at merchants, moving beyond speculation into everyday payments.
Stablecoin adoption is accelerating amid improving regulatory clarity and merchant demand for alternatives to traditional payment networks.
Major retailers are starting to integrate stablecoin payment rails, signaling mainstream acceptance of digital currency for everyday transactions.

items.title: Abstract Shuts Down Despite 400,000 Users
points: Abstract, a consumer Ethereum Layer 2 (blockchain built on top of Ethereum for faster, cheaper transactions), is shutting down December 15 despite onboarding 400,000 users and deploying 144 apps.

It partnered with Red Bull Racing and Disney and built technical standouts like Abstract Global Wallet and the Portal discovery product, but could not sustain operations against better-funded competitors.
Cited reasons include a restricted DeFi ecosystem, thin liquidity, minimal institutional adoption, and budget constraints.
Users must bridge assets via migrate.abs.xyz before December 15 or risk losing access to funds, ending nearly three years of operations.

items.title: Institutional Crypto Expansion: Stablecoins and Tokenized Assets
points: Grayscale's Zcash ETF gathered $1 billion in its first 30 trading days, entering the top 1% of ETF launches in the past decade.

SEC's generic listing standards now cover ~15 tokens beyond bitcoin and ether, letting issuers be selective rather than forcing everything through bitcoin/ether templates; Grayscale filed to tokenize two covered-call funds under an SEC innovation exemption.
Tokenized stocks grew 395% year-over-year to $3.17 billion in supply, while DeFi use of tokenized stocks stayed under 3%.
Sky Protocol became the first stablecoin protocol rated by Moody's (B3 rating, stable outlook), joining a prior S&P rating.

EtherFi launched its own stablecoin (EtherFi USD) using Ethena's Whitelabel infrastructure, shifting crypto neobanks from app-based to company-issued dollar models; EtherFi owns user distribution (300M+ in deposits, 100K+ active cards) but relies on Ethena's yield engine.

items.title: DeFi Infrastructure Advances
points: GSR committed $100 million of its own capital to Hare, an onchain credit desk launching a USD stablecoin yield vault and a tokenized gold (PAXG) yield vault, backed by Aave, Paxos, Chainlink, and Hypernative.

AntSeed built an open inference marketplace on a BitTorrent-style DHT (distributed hash table—decentralized network without central servers), letting AI model providers and consumers trade directly in USDC on Base without a central gatekeeper.

items.title: Security Vulnerabilities: Flash Loans and Cryptography Risks
points: Flash loan attacks (exploits using temporary uncollateralized loans to drain protocols) drained $1.2 billion from DeFi between Feb 2020-Jul 2024, 18.44% of $6.568 billion in total DeFi losses, with Ethereum absorbing 80%.

Four exploit types—price oracle attacks, donate function logic exploits, reentrancy, and governance exploits—drove 81% of cumulative damage; attacks over $10 million accounted for 88% of stolen funds.
Protocol logic exploits grew from 28% of losses (Feb 2020-Jan 2022) to 55% (Feb 2022-Jul 2024), displacing price oracle manipulation as the primary attack vector.

Vitalik Buterin warned AI could accelerate mathematical advances enough to weaken lattice-based cryptography (ML-DSA and FHE—homomorphic encryption, letting computation occur on encrypted data without decryption) within two years, potentially threatening ECDSA sooner than expected.

items.title: Encrypted Mempools and Accountability Research
points: Researchers proposed a traitor-tracing mechanism for encrypted mempools to identify committee members leaking threshold decryption key shares, adapting threshold Paillier encryption and Shamir secret sharing to close MEV (maximum extractable value—profits from ordering/manipulating transactions) accountability gaps.

Three limitations constrain deployment: a trusted setup authority retains decrypt ability, tracing fails against stateful decoder boxes, and factoring-based cryptographic assumptions remain vulnerable to quantum computers—marking preliminary theoretical progress rather than production-ready infrastructure.
